test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How did the Bombay and Madras governments respond to the proposal of the 1839 Draft Act on slavery?

options.text: Both supported the Act without changes
Bombay supported it, Madras rejected it
Bombay saw no need for a law; Madras questioned its expediency
Both governments demanded full enforcement of the Act

solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay saw no need for a law; Madras questioned its expediency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The 1839 Draft Act on Slavery was proposed to address the issue of slavery in India during the British colonial period.
 
• The Bombay government expressed that it did not see the necessity for a law to address slavery, as they believed the issue did not require legislative intervention. ***Hence, this part of the statement is correct.***
 
• The Madras government, on the other hand, questioned the expediency of the draft act. They were concerned about the practicality and implications of implementing such a law. ***This part of the statement is also correct.***
 
• The divergence in opinion highlighted the different administrative perspectives and priorities of the two presidencies under British rule.
 
• This disagreement delayed the consensus on anti-slavery measures and revealed the complexities of governance in colonial India.
